changes.summary: AccountFactsAccumulator replays return floats from an auto-deleted temporary file in 64 KiB buffered writes, preserving multi-pass exact metrics while removing the O(n) Python float list. Optional max_return_count rejects before accumulator state advances.
Added a 4,096-return exact parity check between disk-backed and in-memory metrics, spool-size assertion, and return-count rejection state-integrity regression.

verification.pytest_command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_historical_factory.py tests/test_native_report_accumulator_parity.py tests/test_native_decimal_arithmetic.py tests/test_research_metrics.py tests/test_native_liquidation_facts.py --basetemp .tmp_backup_final_pytest_20261023
verification.mypy_result: Success: no issues found in 3 source files

storage_microbenchmark.method: Synthetic sine-wave floats, Python tracemalloc, isolated list construction versus buffered disk-sequence append. This measures return storage only, not full account-row processing or final metric replay.

metric_replay_microbenchmark.method: The same synthetic returns were evaluated by series_metrics from a list and from the disk-backed replay sequence. tracemalloc began after the original input list and spool were built, so this compares additional metric-calculation allocation and excludes retained-input memory.

environment_boundary: Python 3.14.7 and tooling were invoked from the main project's existing .venv without installing or changing packages. RouteB source was loaded via PYTHONPATH and MYPYPATH. This is not a RouteB-isolated environment verification.
data_boundary: Synthetic account equity rows only; no market, Validation, Test, or Holdout payload was read.
remaining_f7_limits: Full account rows remain materialized when explicitly requested. Tail risk uses a heap proportional to the configured tail fraction at report time; this is not constant-memory independent of the configured maximum return count. The 200,000-return measurements show 96.6% lower storage-build peak memory at 2.36x append latency, and 50.2% lower additional metric-calculation peak memory at 1.28x latency; both are synthetic microbenchmarks, not full workload profiles. Real-history Train profile and clean Hosted Linux/Windows CI remain incomplete.
